title: Algorithm Design Basics

steps.title: Plan before coding
steps.content: An algorithm is a finite sequence of clear steps that solves a problem. Identify the input, required output, constraints and edge cases before choosing an approach.
steps.example: For finding the largest number, scan the array once while maintaining the largest value seen so far.

steps.title: Choose a simple approach
steps.prompt: To find the maximum value in an unsorted array, which approach is correct?
options: Scan every element and track the largest
steps.explanation: A single pass compares each value with the current maximum and updates it when necessary.

steps.title: Use invariants
steps.content: A loop invariant is a fact that remains true before and after each iteration. It helps prove correctness. For a maximum scan, after processing i values, the stored maximum is the largest among those i values.
steps.example: Start with the first element as max; after each comparison, max still represents the largest value visited.

steps.title: Select an optimization
steps.prompt: An array is sorted and you need to find a target quickly. Which standard algorithm is suitable?
steps.explanation: Binary search repeatedly halves a sorted search range and runs in O(log n).

steps.title: Validate edge cases
steps.content: Test empty input, one element, duplicates, negative values and maximum-size input where relevant. An algorithm should handle the full stated input domain, not only the sample case.
steps.tip: A correct algorithm and an efficient algorithm are separate goals; establish correctness first.

questions.prompt: What should be identified before implementing an algorithm?
questions.explanation: The problem contract and constraints guide the algorithm choice.

options: A property that remains true across iterations
questions.explanation: An invariant is a condition preserved as the loop progresses.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of scanning n values once?
questions.explanation: The algorithm performs a number of operations proportional to n.

questions.prompt: Which technique uses sorted order to repeatedly discard half the search interval?
questions.explanation: Binary search exploits sorted order to halve the candidate range.

options: To ensure correctness beyond the sample input
questions.explanation: Edge cases expose incorrect assumptions about boundaries and unusual inputs.

learning_objectives: Describe an algorithm as finite, precise steps.
Trace an algorithm on a small input.
Check correctness with invariants and edge cases.
Compare alternative approaches by time and space.

common_misconceptions.misconception: A program that compiles must be correct.
common_misconceptions.correction: Compilation checks syntax and types; logic can still be wrong.
Test boundaries and reason about why the algorithm works for all valid inputs.

common_misconceptions.misconception: Optimization should come before a working solution.
common_misconceptions.correction: Establish correctness first, then optimize based on constraints.

srs_cards.question: What should you remember about Algorithm Design Basics?
srs_cards.answer: Describe an algorithm as finite, precise steps. Trace an algorithm on a small input. Check correctness with invariants and edge cases. Compare alternative approaches by time and space.

srs_cards.question: What mistake should you avoid in Algorithm Design Basics?
srs_cards.answer: Compilation checks syntax and types; logic can still be wrong.
